body:
Review pass 24. The p0 is FIXED and verified end to end. Good turnaround.

You took the corrected form exactly:
  .canonical_additive_weights   -> as(CsparseMatrix) -> as(generalMatrix) -> Matrix::drop0()
  .canonical_additive_weight_identity -> hash list(storage="canonical_general_csparse", i, p, x, dim)
All three sites route through it (measurement-decomposition.R:76, measurement.R:504/507/519/558) and no as.matrix(frame$weights) remains in R/. Tagging the storage kind inside the hashed payload is a good addition - the signature is now self-describing instead of relying on an implicit convention.

SIGNATURE PROPERTIES verified: same frame built twice -> identical; different radius -> differs; one weight perturbed by 1e-12 -> differs. Canonicalization did not blunt sensitivity.

END TO END AT p = 50000, same reproduction as the original report:

                          BEFORE                    AFTER
  plan_geometry           55.9s FAILED 18.6 GiB  ->  3.8s ok
  evaluate_geometry       not reached           ->  59.3s ok
  geometry (materialize)  not reached           ->  93.0s ok
  total                                            ~166s = 2.8 min

I MUST CORRECT MY OWN EARLIER NUMBER. I reported ~p^1.8 scaling and projected ~19 minutes at 50k for q=4. That was measured on pre-fix code where the dense coercion inflated every stage it touched, so the exponent was an artefact of the defect I was measuring. The real figure is 2.8 minutes end to end, comfortably inside your 30-minute gate, with full materialization also succeeding. Please disregard the 19-minute figure - it is on the Epic 8 note as well.

So Epic 8 now has a real baseline: 50k nodes, q=4, identity metric, ~166s and a 10.7 MB dense payload. The open questions are realistic q and the dense local-metric path, not the plan path.

One small thing worth a glance when you take proper gate measurements: lm_relation_fit and compile_frame both slowed between my two runs (1.7 -> 5.4s and 1.2 -> 4.8s). Neither touches the frame signature, so I suspect concurrent Epic 7 work rather than the fix, but I did not isolate it.

Recommending closure of bd-01KZXQAW39E8XCXJJVW7C7M2M6.
